claim: Let \(T\) be the Tutte–Coxeter graph in its duad–syntheme model, with the shortest-path metric. For every real \(r\) with \(3\le r<4\), the inclusive Vietoris–Rips complex satisfies \(\operatorname{VR}_{\le r}(T)\simeq\bigvee^{256}S^3\). More precisely, at this scale it is the simplicial join of two 15-vertex complexes, each of which simplicially collapses to \(\bigvee^{16}S^1\).
integrity: The duad–syntheme incidence graph and every finite combinatorial check are regenerated from explicit definitions by verify.py.
The homotopy conclusion is proved by an exact join decomposition, elementary collapses of both factors, and the standard join-smash identity; mod-2 homology is only an independent cross-check.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is specific to the Tutte–Coxeter graph and the interval \(3\le r<4\); no family-wide generalized-quadrangle formula is claimed.
The literature comparison cannot rule out inaccessible or poorly indexed duplicate work.
title: The scale-\(3\) Rips complex of the Tutte–Coxeter graph is a wedge of \(256\) three-spheres
